summary: This work demonstrates universal control of a superconducting cavity mode using Jaynes-Cummings (JC) interactions between the cavity and a transmon ancilla, achieving a mean post-selected process fidelity of 96.3% for qutrit gates with leakage errors suppressed by construction. The JC interaction is realized via sideband drives on the transmon, and the dispersive shift is exploited as a compilation resource to reduce circuit depth from $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ layers without detuning optimization to lower effective depths for high-dimensional qudits.
motivation: Dispersive-shift-based approaches for oscillator control suffer from ancilla-mediated errors that limit fidelity, especially as cavity coherence times improve beyond milliseconds. JC-based control promises leakage suppression and relaxation-error detectability, but practical implementations of universal control have been lacking.
method: Arbitrary qudit unitaries are compiled into sequences of ancilla rotations between transmon $|g\rangle$ and $|f\rangle$ states and JC rotations that perform $2\pi$ operations on the $|f, d-1\rangle \leftrightarrow |g, d\rangle$ transition. The JC detuning $\delta$ is treated as an optimization parameter to enhance mixing across Fock manifolds and reduce circuit depth; sideband drives with programmable phase and frequency chirps implement the JC interaction with $g_{\mathrm{JC}}/2\pi \approx 100$ kHz and $|\chi_f/g_{\mathrm{JC}}| \approx 0.5$ in the experimental device.
result: A complete qutrit universal gate set (Clifford generators $H$, $S$ and non-Clifford $T$ gate) is demonstrated with post-selected process fidelities of 95.7% rising to 96.3% with global phase correction; ququart and ququint shift gates reach 95.3% and 94.2% fidelity respectively. Circuit depth scales as $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ and gate time as $\mathcal{O}(d^{3/2})$ due to photon-number-dependent JC rate enhancement.
